description: Rendering spin for the city simulation: a real three.js spin-ui:// viewer for physics-test's synthetic scene (subscribes to position/orientation/physics_lod_tier/shape/radius/half_extents, no enumeration, pure subscribe-by-name), with one real adaptive-fidelity mechanism (full geometry for 'full' LOD tier bodies, cheap impostors for 'kinematic' tier bodies) and its own settings panel (quality preset, DXGI-enumerated compute device choice, remote-compute stub, city area picker, Cesium ion token, grid line color). Also draws city-roads/city-buildings' real OpenStreetMap Klosterneuburg extract (real road lines, basic extruded building footprints, AI-classified wall materials) plus agent-behavior-test's own moving walker/vehicle markers. Three switchable views, each a real Core-backed render_settings.view_mode (survives reload): a vector scene, a Photorealistic mode with real Google Photorealistic 3D Tiles via CesiumJS + a user's own Cesium ion token, and a new Grid view (pure wireframe/edges-only, one configurable line color) with real drag-to-move building repositioning that regenerates affected roads live. Every building, agent, and physics body in the scene is click-selectable (a real raycast against each one's own mesh) and opens a generic property-inspector panel listing EVERY real Core attribute that entity currently has, editable in place. Includes a built-in AI analyst panel (ai-test request/response round trip) for asking real questions about the live city data (traffic, materials, road proximity) with user-toggleable context layers. Not the eventual GTA6-style adaptive renderer — no ray tracing, no temporal denoising.
author: prackoreal
